pf.license.need: Usually none: most states license neither dog walking nor pet sitting. Some cities ask for a permit to walk dogs for pay, or to walk several dogs at once in a park. Carrying dogs in a van can need a pet transport license where the state's rules require one. The state's or city's form says which.
pf.license.ask: The business registration or local business license number, where the form asks for one. A city dog-walking permit, or a pet transport license for van pick-ups, where the form asks for it.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. A city permit to walk dogs in its parks can be per walker, where the city's form says so.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.insurance_bond: Pet-care liability insurance or a bond is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.not_this_work: Dog training, grooming, boarding at the business and vet care are other kinds of work, with their own plug-ins.

pf.first_steps.group_check: Group walks and hikes: a new dog joins only after a free 20-minute group check at the meeting spot, at least 1 day before (the example), and with rabies and DHPP on file.
pf.first_steps.plan: A weekly plan starts after the meet-and-greet. It gets its own yes. If the meet-and-greet finds the dog isn't a fit, the plan ends before any walk, with nothing charged.

pf.visit.check_in: Walks and drop-ins: nobody home, no code. The walker opens the lockbox and texts DONE with the walk report and a photo. When the customer is home, the code at the door works as usual. The meet-and-greet is with the customer home. At the meeting spot: the code is given at drop-off, and again at pick-up.
pf.visit.entry_codes: Shown only to the walker on the job, only during the walk window. Each opening is logged. Deleted 72 hours after the plan ends.
pf.visit.lockout: The lockbox or door code fails: the walker texts it, the customer gets a link to fix it on the secure page, and the walker waits 10 minutes (the example), then leaves. A fee, never more than the walk's price, only if the owner confirms.
pf.visit.walk_report: Times in and out, pee and poop, water filled, the door locked, any notes, and a photo.
pf.visit.pick_up: At the meeting spot, a dog goes home only with the customer's code, or with someone the customer named who shows an ID.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: A longer walk or an extra dog only when the customer asks, priced from the list first.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE with the walk report and a photo.
pf.visit.weather: Ice, lightning, heat over the owner's limit or deep cold: a 10-minute potty break and play inside, same price, or a free skip. The customer picks; the business's call never costs more.

pf.money.start: Walks: a card saved at booking, and each walk charged to it at DONE. Sam can bill the week's walks on Friday instead. A one-time walk is paid in full when booked. The meet-and-greet and the group check are free. At the meeting spot: a trail hike is paid in full when booked; a group walk saves a card and is charged at pick-up.
pf.money.deposits: None. Nothing is held for a walk.
pf.money.fees: A late skip (the example: after 8pm the night before) or no way in: up to the walk's own price, $28, only if the owner confirms. A late cancel or no-show at the meeting spot: $20 (the example). No answer, no fee. A change the business makes never costs the customer.
pf.money.plans: Each plan walk is charged at its own DONE. Or Sam bills the week's walks on Friday, after the last walk, told the day before. Rosfield's $2 counts once a month for a plan.
pf.money.vet_care: Emergency vet care is paid by the customer, up to the limit they signed. It never goes through Rosie.
pf.money.tips: Optional, all to the walker. A tip line only if the owner turns it on.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes pet services, from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking, once a month for a plan.

pf.rules.local_rules: Leash laws, waste pick-up and limits on dogs per walker in parks, as the city's form sets them.

matter_most: A lost dog, a bite or an injury on a walk: the owner and the customer are told at once. The business handles it; Rosie never admits fault or offers money.
Lockout: a lockbox or door code that fails. The walker waits 10 minutes, then leaves; the owner decides any fee.
A walker is out: someone the customer hasn't met goes in only after the customer's OK. No reply: the owner calls first, or a free skip.
Weather day: ice, lightning, heat or deep cold turns a walk into a short potty break and play inside, same price, or a free skip.
Skip, pause or end a plan. A skip after the cut-off may be charged, only if the owner confirms.
The meet-and-greet finds the dog isn't a fit, or fits solo walks only.
Several open walks in a plan's week: which one is asked first.
A dog not picked up at the meeting spot on time.
A vaccine record runs out: group walks and hikes stop until a new one is on file.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
From the cleaner pilot: dog walking runs the same way as home cleaning. The walker comes to an empty home on a weekly plan, gets in with a lockbox or a door code, and a stand-in needs the customer's OK. The cleaner's lockbox, plan and stand-in ops were the starting point; every pilot word was replaced.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Dog Walking. Alex books Biscuit, a beagle mix, at 31 Maple Ave: a free meet-and-greet at home Tue Oct 20 at 5:30pm (a required first step), then 30-minute walks with Devon on weekdays, 11am to 1pm, from Thu Oct 22, with nobody home. Devon texts DONE with a walk report and a photo. Second kind of work: pet sitting (drop-ins and overnights), with no license.
Flow A is the less usual side, from the old flowchart's group walks and van pick-up: Lee Pack Hikes, Sam's second company. Alex drops Biscuit at the base, 120 Ridge Rd, for a 1-hour group walk Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am, after a free group check Fri Oct 23 at 5:30pm. Pick-up is at 12:00pm with the check-in code. Drop-off slots name no hike leader, up to 4 dogs a leader.
Names: Jordan and Casey become dog walkers Devon and Luca; Riley and Avery become hike leaders Sage and Mika. Jamie becomes Ellis. Neutral names, so every he, she or they still fits.
Prices: $28 solo walk (the old flowchart's own price), $42 one-time 60-minute walk, $8 extra dog, $10 holiday add-on, $22 short visit, $30 drop-in, $95 overnight. Lee Pack Hikes: $35 group walk, $75 with a van pick-up, $40 90-minute group walk, $25 puppy walk, $55 trail hike, $20 paw rinse, $140 full-day trip, group check free. Lee Dog Walking's fee for a late skip or no way in is the walk's own $28; Lee Pack Hikes' no-show or late-cancel fee is $20. Each is charged only after Sam's yes.
Money paths, and why each is real. B list|card|card (main): a card saved at booking, charged $28 at each DONE, the way plan walks are usually paid. B list|none|bill: a walk with nothing taken, billed by text after, for customers who pay by link, cash or check. B list|full|none: the one-time 60-minute walk, paid in full when booked, since there's no plan. A list|card|card (main): the group walk, card charged at pick-up. A list|full|none: the trail hike (and van pick-up group walk, full-day trip), paid in full when booked. No holds or deposits anywhere, so the sign-up words (S1-13 to S1-16, S1-41 to S1-47) and S11-56 were rewritten to say so.

The main story charges at each DONE instead (the master's card path); a weekly plan charge is the B7-52 what-if: told Thursday, charged Friday after the week's last walk, the old flowchart's way (B9-22 on the bill path).
